title: Find RFAs by status and age
description: Start with the overview, narrow the list, and open the treatment that needs attention.
before: Open Requests for authorization in your workspace. The RFA feature must be enabled for your organization.
You need permission to read RFAs. Counts and available actions depend on your workspace.
Aging counts calendar days since submission. Decision due uses the review clock after receipt of the complete request; these are separate dates.

Standard prospective/concurrent review generally allows 5 business days; qualifying expedited review allows 72 elapsed hours; retrospective review allows 30 calendar days. Special review rules, incomplete requests, and documented extensions can change the deadline.

For standard electronic submissions, after-hours transmission can move effective receipt to the next business day; expedited and concurrent requests have exceptions. For ordinary mail without receipt evidence, the receipt presumption generally starts five business days after documented mailing. A certified return receipt supplies the actual receipt date. Do not substitute the submission date for receipt evidence.

steps.title: Start with the overview
steps.instruction: Select Overview. The dashboard groups requests into Needs attention (1), Awaiting decision (2), and Finished (3).
steps.expected: Incomplete and Failed requests need attention. Sent and Received requests await decisions. Closed and Canceled requests appear under Finished. Aging shows calendar days since submission, not the utilization review deadline.
steps.alt: The three status groups and their aging columns
steps.caption: Each outlined group contains related statuses. The example has six fictional requests.

steps.title: Choose a status and age range
steps.instruction: Select a count in an aging column. Here, select Received requests aged 15–30 days (1).
steps.expected: The RFAs list opens with both the selected status and age range applied.
steps.alt: Received count for requests aged 15 to 30 days
steps.caption: The highlighted count is an interactive filter.

steps.title: Open a matching request
steps.instruction: Check the Status filter (1) and age range above the table, then select Review request (2).
steps.expected: The detail page opens for the selected RFA. You can review its treatments, documents, history, and available actions.
steps.alt: Filtered requests and Review request control
steps.caption: Status and aging filters narrow the list together.

steps.title: Search as you type
steps.instruction: Enter a patient, physician, claim, RFA, service, or code in Search requests (1). Pause briefly to see results. Clear filters (2) removes the search, status, and aging selection.
steps.expected: The search updates after a short pause without a Search button. The dashboard also refreshes automatically while open and when you return to it.
steps.caption: Search is debounced. Background updates poll every 30 seconds and on return to the page.

steps.title: Switch to individual treatments
steps.instruction: Select Requested treatments (1). Select a treatment’s request link (2) to open its RFA at that treatment. Check Decision due (3) separately from submission age.
steps.expected: The treatment table retains the current search and filters and shows service, diagnosis, decision, and any recorded deadline. Pagination moves between requests, which can each contain multiple treatments. Day-based deadlines display in Pacific time; expedited deadlines include the time. Awaiting receipt means receipt evidence is missing. Not calculated means no usable deadline was returned; review the request’s timeline and deadline basis.
steps.alt: Requested treatments tab and request link
steps.caption: The synthetic request was received September 1, 2026; its five-business-day example is due September 9, excluding Labor Day. The screenshot verifies display, not backend calculation.

limitations: The status and aging drilldown, debounced search request, and treatment navigation were exercised against the synthetic fixture.

related.label: California RFA receipt and delivery rules

title: Read history and delivery evidence
description: Review who did what, add follow-up context, and find saved transmission evidence.
before: Open an RFA with Review request and find Treatments and history.
Reading history requires RFA read access. Adding a note requires the corresponding write permission.

steps.title: Review events and follow-up notes
steps.instruction: In History and notes, read the dated events and recorded actors. Expand Event details where available. To add context, enter a Note (1) and select Save note (2).
steps.expected: Events identify their associated treatment when relevant. A saved note adds context to history; it does not change a treatment decision.
steps.caption: This capture verifies history rendering and note controls; saving a note was not exercised in this run.

steps.title: Inspect delivery evidence
steps.instruction: Open Delivery evidence. Review the recorded channel, status, time, recipient, and reference. When available, select Download transmission receipt (1).
steps.expected: A saved transmission record and its receipt provide delivery evidence. The treatment’s decision remains a separate record: delivery alone does not establish authorization.
steps.alt: Delivery evidence and transmission receipt control
steps.caption: The illustrated transmission and receipt are synthetic. Receipt downloading was not exercised.

limitations: History and delivery records were rendered from fixtures. Note saving and receipt downloading are pictured controls, not verified backend operations in this capture run.

title: Close or reopen treatment follow-up
description: Stop waiting for a decision that is no longer needed, with a reason recorded for the individual treatment.
before: Open the RFA and find the pending treatment under Treatments and history.
You need permission to update the RFA. Use this action only when an outstanding treatment decision is no longer needed.
This closes internal follow-up. It does not record approval or denial and does not withdraw the request with the claims administrator.

steps.title: Close follow-up for one treatment
steps.instruction: Expand Decision no longer required. Enter a specific reason (1), then select Close treatment (2).
steps.expected: The treatment shows Decision no longer required, who closed it, when, and why. Other treatments remain independent. When every treatment has a decision or closed follow-up, the RFA can become Closed.
steps.alt: Closure reason and Close treatment control
steps.caption: Close the treatment that no longer needs a decision, rather than changing its clinical outcome.

steps.title: Reopen if follow-up becomes necessary
steps.instruction: Expand Reopen treatment follow-up. Enter the reason (1), then select Reopen treatment (2).
steps.expected: Follow-up resumes with the original review deadline. Reopening does not start a new review period or erase another treatment’s outcome.
steps.alt: Reopening reason and Reopen treatment control
steps.caption: The earlier closure reason remains visible before reopening.

steps.title: Check the reopened treatment
steps.instruction: Confirm the returned treatment state and reopening reason. The Decision no longer required control (1) becomes available again.
steps.expected: The treatment is pending again and shows who reopened it and why. Its clinical decision remains unchanged throughout closing and reopening.
steps.caption: This is the visible result returned after the synthetic reopen request.

limitations: Both close and reopen PATCH requests were exercised against the fixture and their returned UI states were checked. These screenshots do not independently verify persistence in a production database.
